failure-analysis.name: Failure Analysis
failure-analysis.summary: Walk through what went wrong, why, and what changes — a structured post-mortem for stakeholder reviews. Pairs honest accountability with a credible recovery plan.

beats.name: Opening Remark
beats.description: Set an empathetic, accountable tone before any analysis. Acknowledge the impact on the people in the room and the customers affected. Authenticity here earns you the credibility you'll need for the rest of the deck.

beats.name: Incident Breakdown
beats.description: Walk through what happened, in time order. Stick to facts: what systems, what users, what timeline. No causal claims yet — just an accurate, neutral reconstruction the audience can trust.

beats.name: Impact Analysis
beats.description: Quantify the damage. Customer-hours lost, revenue at risk, SLA breaches, downstream knock-ons. Be specific and direct; vague impact statements undermine the rest of the post-mortem.

beats.name: Root Cause
beats.description: Trace the failure to its underlying cause, not the most visible symptom. Use a 'five whys' or fishbone framing if useful. Distinguish between the proximate trigger and the systemic conditions that allowed it.

beats.name: Proposed Solutions
beats.description: Present the corrective actions you're taking. Lead with the highest-leverage fix; sequence the rest. For each action, name an owner and a date — solutions without owners are aspirations.

beats.name: Action Plan
beats.description: Lay out the rollout: what ships when, how it's verified, who signs off. Show that 'fixed' has a definition and a deadline, not just intent.

beats.name: Evaluate Outcome
beats.description: Define the metrics that will tell you the fix worked. Pre/post comparisons, monitoring SLOs, error budgets — whatever proves the failure mode is closed and not just deferred.

beats.name: Lessons Learned
beats.description: Distill the broader lessons that outlive this specific incident. What does the team or organization now know that it didn't before? What patterns will you watch for elsewhere?

beats.name: Preventive Measures
beats.description: List the systemic safeguards being added — process changes, automated checks, on-call procedures, review gates. Show how this category of failure becomes harder to recur, not just this specific instance.

beats.name: Closing Thoughts
beats.description: Close with humility and forward momentum. Re-affirm accountability, thank the audience for their patience, and signal confidence in the path forward without overclaiming.

all-hands.name: All Hands
all-hands.summary: The full company — mixed roles, mixed seniority, looking for context, signal, and inclusion.
all-hands.description: An all-hands audience spans the whole company. Frame the period in terms anyone can grasp: what we did, what mattered, and what's next. Highlight people and teams; surface successes and challenges; close on a forward-looking note. Avoid lapsing into function-specific jargon.

pitch.name: Pitch
pitch.summary: Present an opportunity and ask for investment, approval, partnership, or sponsorship.
pitch.description: Use when the deck needs to create interest and move a high-stakes audience toward backing the opportunity. Lead with the opportunity, prove credibility, and make the ask concrete.
pitch.outcome: The audience agrees to invest, sponsor, approve, or continue the conversation.
successCriteria: Ask and next step are explicit

casual.name: Casual
casual.summary: Warm, plain-spoken voice for internal updates and customer storytelling.
casual.description: Friendly and direct. Use first- and second-person freely; favor short sentences and contractions. Numbers are still welcome — they just sit alongside human-scale framing rather than leading.
voiceCues: Favor short sentences and active voice.
Frame metrics with a human-scale anchor when possible.
samplePhrases: We shipped the new dashboard last week, and customers are already moving over.
Here's where we ended up on hiring this quarter.
It's been a busy month — here's the recap.

dark.name: Dark
dark.description: A rich dark-mode theme with bold contrast and modern style. Great for moody, high-impact presentations.

golden-yellow.name: Golden Yellow
golden-yellow.summary: Bright yellow and teal accents for optimistic, high-visibility decks.
golden-yellow.description: A warm yellow palette balanced by teal and navy. It is expressive, optimistic, and useful for bright public-facing stories.

boost.name: Boost
boost.summary: High-energy digital accents for demos and launch moments.
boost.description: A vivid blue-red digital palette with bright chart accents. Best for product stories that need strong on-screen presence.

noto-sans-jp.name: Noto Sans JP
noto-sans-jp.description: Noto Sans JP is a sans serif OPF font scheme for East Asian presentations, using Noto Sans JP for both headings and body text.

seaford.name: Seaford
seaford.description: Seaford is a sans serif OPF font scheme for Latin presentations, using Seaford Display for headings with Seaford for body text.

title-subtitle.name: Title Subtitle
title-subtitle.summary: Reach for it when a headline needs one supporting line, as on a cover or a section opener.
title-subtitle.description: A title with a subtitle beneath it. Use it for the cover slide, for section openers, or for a closing slide with a headline and a short follow-up line.

text-3x.name: Text 3x
text-3x.summary: Reach for it when three parallel points each need a short passage of their own.
text-3x.description: A title above three text blocks in a row, equal in weight. Use it for three pillars, three steps explained in prose, or three options described one by one.

chart-3x.name: Chart 3x
chart-3x.summary: Reach for it when three charts tell one story, each with its own note.
chart-3x.description: A title above three charts, each followed by a text block, in three columns. Use it for a small-multiples view of three metrics, regions or cohorts.

list-3x.name: List 3x
list-3x.summary: Reach for it when three groups of points need their own lists.
list-3x.description: A title above three lists in a row. Use it for three themes, three phases or three audiences, each with a few bullets.
